title: Intrinsic adic geometric fibres and their finite-stage normalization
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a scheme $W$, an algebraically closed field $K$ and a geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to W$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its common finite-stage coefficient category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For every finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], define the integral geometric fibre on the intrinsic derived-complete constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] by its inclusion into the ambient derived category, the constant-section-normalized coefficient-model equivalence [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport], actual completed geometric pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], degree-zero cohomology, point sections, and scalar extension $\mathcal O_E\to E$. Define its rational fibre to be the unique descent along the intrinsic rational localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], characterized by equality of its composite with localization and that integral fibre, including all fraction maps. For a finite coefficient subfield $L\subset\Omega$, define the coefficient embedding from its small model to $\Omega$ to be the composite of the canonical $\operatorname{Shrink}$ algebra equivalence with the subfield inclusion. A functor $F:\mathcal C_W(\Omega)\to\operatorname{Mod}_\Omega$ satisfies the intrinsic common-stage fibre specification if, for every such $L$, its composite with the stage inclusion is naturally isomorphic to the rational fibre at $L$, followed by scalar extension along that actual coefficient embedding. This is only the normalization predicate; existence, exactness and conservativity of a common-stage fibre are separate assertions.
